digest.component_or_area: completion verification agent step, LLM workflow runner
propositions: The primary completion-verify agent step is dispatched with no tool_step_limit, so budget exhaustion kills the run with no verdict instead of landing one.
Repetitive tool-call cycles (k-cycles with k >= 2) are not detected during execution because max_consecutive_repeat only counts adjacent identical signatures and misses non-adjacent cycles.

When a runaway is detected, it must route to bounded recovery with synthetic steering (synthetic tool results, not tool withdrawal) to avoid provider protocol errors (Bedrock/Anthropic require toolConfig when history contains tool_use).
Budget exhaustion raises UsageLimitExceeded → LLMRunnerError, but CompletionAgentStep.run catches only UnretryableOutputError, so bounded recovery is unreachable and failure_diagnostic is discarded.

A windowed distinct-ratio discriminator (window=24, trip at ≤0.50, order-insensitive) separates pathological loops from healthy breadth with a ~5x safety margin and fires on real multi-signature cycles.

Four independent force-close incidents confirm this is a blocking defect: e369 (59 descendants), aec1 (4 files, 222x identical call), 895c (4 files, 175x identical call), and historical epics 1d96/bf50.
